text: M. Fathima Beevi (30 April 1927 – 23 November 2023) was an Indian judge who served as a justice of the Supreme Court of India. Appointed to the apex court in 1989, she became the first female judge of the Supreme Court of India and the first Muslim woman to be appointed to any of the higher judiciaries in the country. She retired from the Supreme Court on 29 April 1992. After her retirement, she served as a member of the National Human Rights Commission and later as the Governor of Tamil Nadu from 25 January 1997 to 2001. In 2023, she was honoured with the Kerala Prabha Award, the second-highest honour given by the Government of Kerala, and posthumously awarded the Padma Bhushan in the 2024 honours list. Born on 30 April 1927 in Pathanamthitta, then part of the Kingdom of Travancore (now in Kerala), she was the daughter of Annaveettil Meer Sahib and Khadeeja Beevi, belonging to the Rowther family. She attended Town School and Catholicate High School in Pathanamthitta, earned a BSc in chemistry from Women's College, Thiruvananthapuram, and obtained her LL.B. from Government Law College, Thiruvananthapuram. Enrolled as an Advocate on 14 November 1950, she topped the Bar Council exam that year and began her career in the lower judiciary in Kerala, becoming Munsiff in May 1958, Sub-ordinate Judge in 1968, Chief Judicial Magistrate in 1972, and District & Sessions Judge in 1974. In January 1980, she was appointed Judicial Member of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, and elevated to the High Court as a Judge on 4 August 1983. She became a permanent Judge of the High Court on 14 May 1984 and retired from the High Court on 29 April 1989. As Governor of Tamil Nadu, she rejected mercy petitions filed by four condemned prisoners in the Rajiv Gandhi assassination case, invoking her power under Article 161 of the Constitution. She faced controversy for giving a clean chit to the law and order situation in Tamil Nadu, prompting the Central government to request her resignation. She resigned under controversial circumstances after accepting Jayalalithaa's assembly majority following the May 2001 elections and over the arrest of former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi, who had previously advocated for her appointment. Jayalalithaa defended her decision, stating that as a former Supreme Court judge and legal expert, she did not require instruction on law or the Constitution, and her decision was not justiciable. Despite not being eligible to contest an election under constitutional provisions, Fathima Beevi administered the oath of office to J. Jayalalitha as Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on 14 May 2001, based on the majority party's election of her as their leader. Several Public Interest Litigations were filed in the Supreme Court challenging the validity of her appointment, and she justified her action by citing the majority party's election of Jayalalithaa. The Supreme Court later overturned her appointment, ruling that a Governor cannot appoint a non-member of the legislature as Chief Minister, as such an action would be contrary to the Constitution and laws. During her tenure as Governor, she also served as Chancellor of Madras University, where her withholding of approval for the establishment of a new department for contemporary Tamil literature reportedly led to the Vice-Chancellor, P.T. Manoharan, resigning. She had previously served as Chairman of the Kerala Commission for Backward Classes (1993) and member of the National Human Rights Commission (1993), and received the Hon. D. Litt. and Mahila Shiromani Award in 1990, as well as the Bharat Jyoti Award. There were discussions among left parties about her potential nomination as President of India, during which the NDA Government proposed Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. Fathima Beevi passed away on 23 November 2023 at the age of 96.
